[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"On which date did the student community hoist the flag of independent Bangladesh?","marks":1,"answer":"The student community proudly hoisted the flag of independent Bangladesh on March 2, 1971, at Dhaka University. This brave act showed everyone that Bengalis were ready to fight for their freedom and rights.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Why is Bangladesh's Liberation War called 'Ganojudha'? (2)","marks":0,"answer":"The Liberation War is called 'Ganojudha' because people from all walks of life joined together to fight. After the Pakistani army attacked on March 25, 1971, students, farmers, workers, police, women, and even cultural activists all participated. When an entire nation fights together like this, it becomes a people's war or 'Ganojudha'.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Describe the role of the media associated with the person mentioned in the stem. (3)","marks":0,"answer":"Abdul Jabbar worked at Swadhin Bangla Betar Kendra, which was a radio station created during our Liberation War. This radio station played a very important role by broadcasting patriotic songs, news about freedom fighters, and motivational messages. These broadcasts helped keep the spirits of Bengalis high during difficult times. The radio programs made people feel united and brave, even when they were scared. Artists like Abdul Jabbar sang songs that reminded people why they were fighting for independence. The media also helped share important information about the war with people in different areas. Newspapers published by the Mujibnagar Government also spread awareness about our struggle. So, media was like a powerful voice that encouraged everyone to keep fighting for freedom.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"The country played a crucial role in Bangladesh's liberation—analyze this statement. (4)","marks":0,"answer":"The country mentioned in the stem is India, and it truly helped Bangladesh in many important ways during the Liberation War. First, India gave shelter to about one crore Bangladeshi refugees who fled from Pakistani violence. Second, India provided training and weapons to our freedom fighters so they could fight better. Third, Indian media shared stories about Pakistani atrocities with the world, which helped gain international support for Bangladesh. Fourth, the Indian government helped the Mujibnagar Government operate from Kolkata. Fifth, near the end of the war, Indian forces joined with our Muktibahini in a joint command to fight Pakistani soldiers. This teamwork led to Pakistan's surrender on December 16, 1971. India also helped run Swadhin Bangla Betar Kendra and supported our artists. Without India's help in so many areas, our nine-month war for independence would have been much harder. That's why we say India played a crucial role in Bangladesh's liberation.
","image":null,"image_url":null}]

[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What is the Joint Command?","marks":1,"answer":"The Joint Command was the combined military force of Bangladesh's Muktibahini (freedom fighters) and the Indian army that worked together during the final stage of the Liberation War.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Explain the historical significance of the 7 March speech of Bangabandhu. (2)","marks":0,"answer":"Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's speech on March 7, 1971, was very special because it clearly told Bengalis to prepare for independence. Through this speech, he expressed the hopes and dreams of all Bengalis who wanted freedom from Pakistani rule. The speech inspired people to join the non-cooperation movement and get ready for a possible war. It became a guiding light for our freedom struggle.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"The speech by the leader from the "B" area indicates which incident of your textbook? Explain. (3)","marks":0,"answer":"The speech mentioned in the stem refers to Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's historic 7th March speech in 1971. In the stem, "B" area represents East Pakistan (now Bangladesh), which faced discrimination from "A" area (West Pakistan). After winning the 1970 election, the Awami League was not allowed to form the government. When the National Assembly session was postponed, people protested. In this situation, Bangabandhu delivered his famous speech at Racecourse Maidan in Dhaka. He said, "This time the struggle is for our freedom, this time the struggle is for our independence." These words prepared Bengalis mentally and emotionally for the Liberation War. Just like in the stem, the leader inspired people to fight, got arrested, and his companions continued the mission. This exactly matches what happened after March 7, 1971.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Do you think the stem indicates the war-time government of Bangladesh? Give logic in favour of your answer. (4)","marks":0,"answer":"Yes, the stem clearly indicates the Mujibnagar Government, which was Bangladesh's war-time government. After the Pakistani army attacked on March 25, 1971, Bangabandhu was arrested and taken to West Pakistan. But on April 10, 1971, his trusted companions formed a government in Meherpur, naming Bangabandhu as president even though he was in jail. This government had different ministers who handled various responsibilities like finance, foreign affairs, and home affairs. They organized the freedom fighters into sectors, managed refugee issues, and worked to gain international support. Just like in the stem where "wise companions distributed responsibilities," the Mujibnagar Government leaders worked together to run the war effort. They also made Bangabandhu's dream of an independent Bangladesh come true by December 16, 1971. The stem mentions that the leader was arrested but his companions continued his mission, which perfectly matches the historical events of our Liberation War. Therefore, the stem is definitely referring to the Mujibnagar Government.
","image":null,"image_url":null}]

[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What was the percentage of military officers from East Pakistan during the Pakistan period?","marks":1,"answer":"During the Pakistan period, only about 5 percent of military officers were from East Pakistan, which shows the discrimination Bengalis faced in the armed forces.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"What do you know about the 1965 war between India and Pakistan? (2)","marks":0,"answer":"In 1965, India and Pakistan fought a war mainly over the Kashmir region. During this war, East Pakistan (now Bangladesh) was left completely unprotected by the Pakistani government. This showed Bengalis that West Pakistan did not care about their safety, which increased feelings of inequality and helped grow the desire for independence.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"According to the above stem, why was the independence war of X country called Ganojudha? (3)","marks":0,"answer":"The "X" country in the stem is Bangladesh, and its Liberation War is called Ganojudha because people from all backgrounds joined the fight together. When the Pakistani army attacked on March 25, 1971, it wasn't just soldiers who resisted—students, farmers, workers, police, and ordinary citizens all stood up bravely. Women helped by providing food, shelter, and medical care to freedom fighters. Cultural workers sang patriotic songs to keep spirits high. Mass media like Swadhin Bangla Betar spread news and motivation. Immigrant Bengalis abroad raised funds and awareness. Intellectuals wrote articles and gave ideas for the struggle. When everyone in a nation contributes to a war in their own way, it becomes a people's war or 'Ganojudha'. This unity of all classes and professions is what made our Liberation War special and successful.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"According to the stem, analyze "They established the sovereign and independent". (4)","marks":0,"answer":"The statement "They established the sovereign and independent" is absolutely true for Bangladesh's Liberation War. The word "they" refers to all the people of Bangladesh who participated in the war. When the war started, people didn't wait for orders—they took initiative from their own positions. Students left their studies to join freedom fighter camps. Farmers shared their food with fighters. Women provided shelter and nursing care. Cultural activists created songs and plays to boost morale. Intellectuals wrote powerful articles to inspire people. Media workers risked their lives to broadcast the truth. Even Bengalis living abroad organized protests and raised funds. Each group contributed what they could, and together they created a powerful force. This united effort, where everyone sacrificed something for freedom, is what led to Bangladesh becoming an independent country on December 16, 1971. Without this mass participation, victory would not have been possible in just nine months. So yes, it was truly "they"—the people of Bangladesh—who established our sovereign and independent nation through their collective struggle and sacrifice.
","image":null,"image_url":null}]

","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Give details of the progress achieved by Bangladesh as indicated in Robin's speech. (3)","marks":0,"answer":"Robin's speech refers to how Bangladesh has grown stronger by overcoming many challenges with public support. After the 1969 Mass Uprising against Pakistani rule, Bengalis learned the power of unity. This unity helped them win the 1970 election, fight the Liberation War, and build an independent country. Since independence, Bangladesh has made progress in many areas: improving education, growing the economy, developing healthcare, and gaining respect in the international community. Even when facing natural disasters, political challenges, or economic difficulties, the Bangladeshi people have always come together to support their country. This spirit of cooperation, which helped win the Liberation War, continues to help Bangladesh develop today. Robin's message is that as long as people stay united and support each other, Bangladesh can overcome any conspiracy or challenge and keep moving forward.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Analyze the accuracy of the statement made by the brave freedom fighter Mueen Sahib. (4)","marks":0,"answer":"Mueen Sahib's statement is completely accurate because Bangladesh's Liberation War truly became a people's war due to mass participation. When the Pakistani army attacked on March 25, 1971, resistance didn't come only from trained soldiers. Students organized protests and joined freedom fighter camps. Farmers provided food and shelter to fighters. Workers stopped production to hurt the enemy's economy. Women helped in many ways, from nursing wounded fighters to carrying secret messages. Cultural activists created patriotic songs and plays to keep hope alive. Religious leaders encouraged people to fight for justice. Even children helped by passing information. This wide participation from all classes and professions made the war special. Unlike regular wars fought only by armies, our Liberation War involved the entire nation. Every person contributed according to their ability, creating a united front against oppression. This mass involvement is why historians call it 'Ganojudha' or people's war. Without this cooperation from ordinary people, the freedom fighters could not have succeeded in just nine months. Therefore, Mueen Sahib correctly identified that people's cooperation was the key reason our Liberation War took the form of a people's war.

subject: Bangladesh and Global Studies
parts:
[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What is a Ganojudha?","marks":1,"answer":"Ganojudha means a people's war, where citizens from all backgrounds—students, farmers, workers, women, and professionals—join together to fight for their country's freedom.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Why is the night of March 25 called a 'Kalratri'? (2)","marks":0,"answer":"The night of March 25, 1971, is called 'Kalratri' (meaning "night of death") because the Pakistani army launched a brutal attack on innocent Bengalis in Dhaka. They killed students, intellectuals, police, and ordinary people without mercy. This planned genocide, called Operation Searchlight, marked the beginning of our Liberation War and remains a dark memory in our history.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Describe the role of the singer, mentioned in the stem, in Bangladesh's Liberation War. (3)","marks":0,"answer":"The singer mentioned in the stem is George Harrison, a famous British musician. In 1971, he organized a large concert in New York City called "Concert for Bangladesh" to help refugees from our Liberation War. At this concert, he performed a song titled "Bangladesh" that told the world about the suffering of Bengalis under Pakistani rule. The concert raised money that was used to provide food, medicine, and shelter for Bangladeshi refugees in India. Harrison's effort was important because it brought international attention to our struggle when many countries didn't know about the war. His song helped create sympathy for Bangladesh in Western countries. This shows how artists and cultural figures from other nations supported our freedom movement. George Harrison didn't fight with weapons, but he used his talent and fame to help Bangladesh in a meaningful way during our hardest time.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Analyse the statement of the father at the end of the stem. (4)","marks":0,"answer":"The father's statement is correct because many countries did help Bangladesh during the Liberation War. India provided the most direct support by giving shelter to refugees, training freedom fighters, and later joining the war militarily. The Soviet Union supported Bangladesh in the United Nations by using its veto power to stop unfavorable resolutions. Countries like the United Kingdom, France, and Sweden provided humanitarian aid and spoke in favor of Bangladesh internationally. International media outlets like BBC and The New York Times reported on Pakistani atrocities, which helped build global sympathy for our cause. Even ordinary people in different countries organized protests and fundraising events for Bangladesh. This international support was crucial because it isolated Pakistan diplomatically and made it harder for them to continue the war. The father's point that "many other countries also helped" reminds us that Bangladesh's independence wasn't achieved alone—it was supported by a global community that believed in justice and human rights. This international solidarity played an important role in our victory on December 16, 1971.
","image":null,"image_url":null}]

subject: Bangladesh and Global Studies
parts:
[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What was the main objective of the Mujibnagar Government?","marks":1,"answer":"The main objective of the Mujibnagar Government was to lead and organize the Liberation War effectively while also gaining international support and recognition for Bangladesh's independence.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Explain the role of the United Nations in the Liberation War. (2)","marks":0,"answer":"The United Nations mostly remained a silent observer during our Liberation War. Although the UN's goal is to protect world peace, it couldn't stop the genocide that started on March 25, 1971. When Pakistan was losing the war, the US and China proposed a ceasefire in the UN Security Council, but the Soviet Union vetoed it. This shows that the UN's actions were limited by the interests of its powerful member countries.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Explain the structure of the government that is hinted in the stimulus. (3)","marks":0,"answer":"The government hinted at in the stimulus is the Mujibnagar Government, formed on April 10, 1971, in Meherpur. Its structure was well-organized: Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was named President, though he was imprisoned in Pakistan. Syed Nazrul Islam served as Vice President and Acting President. Tajuddin Ahmed was the Prime Minister who led day-to-day operations. M. Mansur Ali handled Finance, A.H.M. Kamaruzzaman managed Home, Relief and Rehabilitation, and Khondoker Mostaq Ahmed took care of Foreign Affairs and Law. This team of elected leaders worked together to run the war effort. They created different ministries to handle various needs like military strategy, refugee care, and international diplomacy. Even though Bangabandhu couldn't be present, the government operated in his name and followed his vision for an independent Bangladesh. This clear structure helped the government function effectively during the difficult war period.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Analyze the activities of that government. (4)","marks":0,"answer":"The Mujibnagar Government carried out many important activities that led to Bangladesh's victory. First, it organized the freedom fighters into 11 military sectors across the country, making resistance more effective. Second, it conducted diplomatic missions worldwide, sending representatives to countries like India, the Soviet Union, and the United States to gain political support. Third, it managed the huge refugee crisis by coordinating with India to provide shelter and aid for millions of displaced Bengalis. Fourth, it ran Swadhin Bangla Betar Kendra to broadcast motivational programs and war news to keep people's spirits high. Fifth, it handled finances by collecting donations and managing resources for the war effort. Sixth, it worked to gain international recognition for Bangladesh, which was crucial for our legitimacy as a new nation. Seventh, it maintained communication between different freedom fighter groups to ensure coordinated attacks. All these activities required careful planning and teamwork. The government's ability to handle military, political, humanitarian, and diplomatic tasks simultaneously showed remarkable leadership. Without this organized government guiding the war effort, the Liberation War might not have succeeded in just nine months. Therefore, the Mujibnagar Government's activities were essential to establishing our independent Bangladesh.
","image":null,"image_url":null}]

They sent money to help refugees and freedom fighters, and they worked to inform the international community about Pakistani atrocities, which helped build global sympathy for our cause.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Explain the role of the community represented by Nadim in the war of liberation. (3)","marks":0,"answer":"Nadim represents the student community, which played a leading role in Bangladesh's Liberation War. When the war began on March 26, 1971, thousands of students left their studies to join the freedom struggle. Many received military training in India and then returned to fight against Pakistani forces. Students formed a large part of the Muktibahini (freedom fighters), especially in the irregular guerrilla units. They organized protests, spread awareness, and motivated others to join the fight. Student groups like Mujib Bahini were created specifically to involve young people in the war effort. Students also helped with intelligence gathering, carrying messages, and providing logistical support. Their energy, courage, and willingness to sacrifice made them a powerful force in the liberation movement. Many student leaders gave their lives for the country, becoming martyrs who inspire us today. Without the active participation of students like Nadim, the Liberation War would have lacked the youthful energy and mass mobilization needed for victory. That's why students are remembered as one of the most important groups in our struggle for independence.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Do you think that the mentioned community only played a role to achieve independence of Bangladesh? Analyze with logics. (4)","marks":0,"answer":"No, the student community was not the only group that played a role in achieving Bangladesh's independence. While students were very important, many other groups contributed significantly too. Political parties, especially the Awami League, provided leadership and organized the overall movement. Farmers and workers supported the war by providing food, shelter, and intelligence to freedom fighters. Women played crucial roles by nursing wounded fighters, carrying secret messages, and even participating in combat after training. Cultural activists used songs, poems, and plays to keep people's spirits high and spread the message of freedom. Religious leaders encouraged people to fight for justice according to their faith. Intellectuals wrote articles and gave speeches that explained why independence was necessary. The media, including Swadhin Bangla Betar, broadcast news and motivational programs. Even children helped by passing information. Each group contributed in their own way based on their abilities. If only students had participated, the war would not have had the broad support needed for victory. It was the combined effort of all these groups—students, farmers, workers, women, intellectuals, and others—that created the people's war (Ganojudha) that successfully liberated Bangladesh. Therefore, while students played a leading role, independence was achieved through the united efforts of the entire Bangladeshi nation.
","image":null,"image_url":null}]

[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"Who was the chief of Pakistan People's Party in 1971?","marks":1,"answer":"The chief of Pakistan People's Party in 1971 was Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, who opposed handing over power to the Awami League after the 1970 election.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"What is "Operation Searchlight"? It involved mass killings of civilians, students, intellectuals, and police in Dhaka and other parts of East Pakistan, marking the start of our Liberation War and a genocide against Bengalis.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Explain the structure and activities of the subject related to our great Liberation War reflected in the stem. (3)","marks":0,"answer":"The stem reflects the formation of the Mujibnagar Government, which was Bangladesh's shadow government during the Liberation War. Its structure included Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman as President, Syed Nazrul Islam as Vice President and Acting President, Tajuddin Ahmed as Prime Minister, and ministers for Finance, Home, and Foreign Affairs. This government was formed on April 10, 1971, with elected representatives from the 1970 election. Its activities were diverse and crucial: it organized freedom fighters into 11 military sectors for effective resistance, conducted diplomatic missions worldwide to gain international support, managed refugee relief efforts with India's help, ran Swadhin Bangla Betar Kendra to broadcast motivational programs, and coordinated military strategies against Pakistani forces. The government also worked to gain recognition for Bangladesh as an independent nation. By handling military, political, humanitarian, and diplomatic tasks simultaneously, the Mujibnagar Government provided the leadership needed to turn the people's agitation into a successful war for independence. This organized structure ensured that the movement mentioned in the stem had clear direction and coordination.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Evaluate the contribution of students, mass people and intellectuals to the Liberation War of Bangladesh as like the movement indicated in the stem. (4)","marks":0,"answer":"The contributions of students, mass people, and intellectuals to Bangladesh's Liberation War were immense and complementary. Students provided energy and courage—they were often the first to protest, joined freedom fighter camps in large numbers, and formed groups like Mujib Bahini. Their willingness to sacrifice inspired others. The mass people, including farmers and workers, formed the backbone of support—they provided food, shelter, and intelligence to freedom fighters, and their widespread participation made the war truly a people's struggle. Intellectuals contributed through ideas and communication—they wrote powerful articles, created patriotic cultural programs, and used media like Swadhin Bangla Betar to keep morale high and spread awareness about the war's purpose. Together, these three groups created a powerful combination: students brought action, mass people brought resources and numbers, and intellectuals brought vision and motivation. This unity across different segments of society is what made the movement in the stem successful. Without students, the resistance might have lacked youthful vigor; without mass people, fighters would have lacked support; without intellectuals, the movement might have lacked clear direction and inspiration. Their combined efforts ensured that the agitation against Pakistani rule transformed into a well-organized war that achieved independence in just nine months. Therefore, evaluating their contributions shows that each group played a unique but equally important role in Bangladesh's freedom struggle.
","image":null,"image_url":null}]

subject: Bangladesh and Global Studies
lesson: Formation and Role of Mujibnagar Government
parts:
[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"Who was the Finance Minister of the Mujibnagar Government?","marks":1,"answer":"M. Mansur Ali was the Finance Minister of the Mujibnagar Government, responsible for managing funds and resources for the Liberation War effort.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"What do you understand by "Operation Searchlight"? (2)","marks":0,"answer":"Operation Searchlight was the code name for the Pakistani army's brutal attack launched on the night of March 25, 1971, to crush the Bengali independence movement. It involved mass killings of civilians, students, intellectuals, and police, marking the start of genocide and our Liberation War.
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"The event discussed in the stem reflects which event of the Liberation War of Bangladesh? Describe its formation. (3)","marks":0,"answer":"The stem reflects the formation of the Mujibnagar Government. After the Awami League won the 1970 election but was not allowed to form the government, and after the Pakistani army's attack on March 25, 1971, Bengali leaders decided to create an independent government. On April 10, 1971, elected representatives gathered in Meherpur and formed the Mujibnagar Government. They named Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman as President (though he was imprisoned in Pakistan), Syed Nazrul Islam as Vice President and Acting President, and appointed Tajuddin Ahmed as Prime Minister along with other ministers for Finance, Home, and Foreign Affairs. This government was formed to provide leadership for the Liberation War, organize resistance efforts, and gain international support.
